mechanism_narrative: When the monthly FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS rises >0.25pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting stronger labor market momentum and investor optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the following month
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation, the effect is insignificant (p > 0.10) or the 20-day forward return is not positive when the threshold is met (empirical frequency < 40%).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly GDPC1 (real personal consumption) exceeds its prior month by at least 1%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating sustained demand growth and upward equity pricing.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥1% in the following month
failure_condition: Over 100 observations where GDPC1 meets the threshold, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% followed by a rebound the next month signals a bottoming out, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market expectations shift to growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥2% then rises in the subsequent month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return occurs in 10 such recovery windows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be negative due to preemptive rate hike anticipation.
failure_condition: Over 50 such episodes, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for three months is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market softness supports rate cut expectations.
failure_condition: Across 20 such softening regimes, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (housing starts) rises by at least 10% in the following month after a negative monthly change, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting optimism about housing recovery and broader economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST negative last month and increases by ≥10% this month
failure_condition: In 30 such recovery windows, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both RSAFS (retail sales) and INDPRO by at least 5% in the same month predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals weak demand and supply contraction, raising recession risk.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS ↓5% and INDPRO ↓5% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 40 such contraction events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
